text:
maria: Heads-up — I pushed a short proposal in the RFC thread: migrate edge telemetry to compact delta envelopes (v2) to cut payload size and avoid duplicating full spans across proxies. Goal: 35-50% payload reduction for hot paths, simpler in-flight dedupe, and clearer per-request cost attribution.
Ajay: Can you sketch how cost attribution stays exact if we only send deltas? worried about double-counting when retries happen.
maria: Good call. Plan is: each envelope carries a canonical request id + monotonic delta sequence + nonce. The ingest layer will rehydrate by applying deltas to a small cache keyed by request id. If a retry arrives with overlapping seq ranges, we dedupe via seq ranges rather than full payload compare.
Kai: Sounds ok but that cache is stateful at ingest — what's the TTL and memory footprint? we can’t blow up the hot path.
maria: TTL 15s by default, bounded LRU with per-shard cap. For large aggregates we fall back to a full-opaque envelope (costly) only when rehydration fails.
Sophia: Migration rollout idea: 1) edge emits both full+delta (dual-write) for 48h on canary region; 2) ingest collects metrics (payload size, rehydration success rate, dedupe events); 3) flip for 10% of global traffic; 4) monitor cost delta vs baseline; 5) full flip + prune dual path after 2 weeks if stable.
Ajay: We should also add a reconciliation query to validate cost neutrality. proposal: nightly job that compares per-request token-count-equivalent across dual-written requests.
Kai: Implementation detail: what about sampling? if edge samples and skips some spans, delta sequences could be missing earlier fragments.
maria: Edge sampling will tag envelopes with sampling-cohort metadata and include a compact map of skipped-starts. Rehydration will tolerate gaps up to N=2 sequences; bigger gaps mark envelope as partial and route to a fallback path that charges to "best-effort" bucket.
observability-bot: deploy-bot: canary gateway v0.3.1 deployed to us-west at 2026-03-23T09:12Z :rocket:
Sophia: For the recon job Ajay suggested, here’s a draft SnQL we can run in baseline timeframe: \n```\nSELECT count() as total, sum(rehydration_failed) as failed FROM telemetry_envelopes WHERE dual_written = true AND ts >= now()-24h GROUP BY shard\n```\nWe’ll compare token proxies and billing_key deltas.
Ajay: Also add a guard: if rehydration_failed_rate > 0.5% in the 1h rolling window, auto-rollback to dual-write for the affected shard.
Kai: Edge case: multi-model routing requests produce interleaved deltas from different downstreams. We need delta seq to be namespaced by model-instance-id to avoid cross-interleaving.
maria: Good catch — we’ll namespace seq by (request_id, model_instance). update RFC patch accordingly.
Sophia: I can own the rollout dashboard (per-shard rehydration %, avg bytes/request, dedupe_events). will share a draft link tomorrow.
Ajay: One more thought — encryption and signing. deltas must be integrity-protected. propose HMAC over the delta blob and include the HMAC header so ingest can validate before applying.
maria: yep will add header `X-RDW-Envelope-Sig: hmac256(...)`. Also a small header for version: `X-RDW-Envelope: compact=v2;delta=true`.
Kai: For the retry semantics, ensure nonces are unique enough (at least 64 bits). collisions -> force opaque fallback.
maria: Agreed. Action items: Sofia (dashboard), Ajay (recon job + auto-rollback guard), Kai (shard cache sizing + namespace change), me (RFC patch: headers, HMAC, TTLs). I'll update the RFC with the timeline and add the canary config. If no major objections by EOD we'll start dual-write canary tomorrow.
Ajay: +1 from me. timeline looks reasonable.
Kai: +1. I’ll run a local sim to estimate memory at scale and report numbers.
Sophia: +1 — will post dashboard link when ready.
maria: thanks — moving to PR.\n\nNotes: keep messages short in the follow-ups; prefer telemetry metrics to be numeric (rates) not heuristic text; watch for backpressure bloom when rehydration cache misses spike.
